source_binding.semantics_used: Page-Hinkley computes observed values and their running mean, implements a CUSUM-style detector, supports downward mean changes, and exposes delta, threshold, and forgetting-factor parameters.
Page-Hinkley is an online concept-drift detector over the observed stream mean with a change threshold; detector state is incremental rather than requiring retained raw history.
River's drift detectors reset internal state after a detected concept drift and PageHinkley supports two-sided tests.

chat_native_reduction.adaptation_note: The Page-Hinkley statistical state is applied only to unique same-scope terminal utility observations. Repository readback identity, scope filtering, historical-evidence qualification, and credit rules are controller guards layered around the public detector rather than claims about the statistical test itself.
rules: For each unique valid observation, update the running mean and the downward Page-Hinkley cumulative statistic; track the running maximum and signal a decrease when max-minus-current exceeds 4.0.
Exclude duplicates, stale observations, scope mismatches, and transport-only events before statistical update.

On the first threshold crossing, append one regime-boundary diagnostic, mark pre-boundary evidence current-ineligible without deleting it, reset detector state at the boundary, and open same-scope re-evaluation.
The detector cannot award assignment credit or select a replacement by itself.
Every detector checkpoint/change boundary is durable/readback-gated; a failed write leaves the prior durable detector state authoritative.
